_note: S181 hardening of the 8 operating_protocol rules that still held VERBATIM INIT-spec text (SPEC-UNIVERSAL-8-UNHARDENED). Hardening standard, uniform across all 8: (a) the spec's intent is preserved, (b) this kernel's field evidence is cited by error/inference id, (c) the rule names the DECIDABLE PREDICATE or the governed verb that decides it -- GATE-OR-HOPE-PRINCIPLE. Values stay UNIVERSAL: mechanism and error-class citations only, no deployment-specific paths (Rule 26 lean_rag_storage).
ask_user_question_echo: After receiving a response from AskUserQuestion (or any structured user-input tool), ECHO THE RECEIVED ANSWER VERBATIM back to the operator in the same turn, BEFORE the first action that depends on it. If the answer is empty or unreadable, ask the operator to paste the value directly in chat -- never infer it. This prevents silent data loss from platform-level parsing failures. HARDENED (S181, from E-092): the echo is necessary but not sufficient. (1) SCOPE OF THE ASK -- consultation is for RULINGS BETWEEN REAL ALTERNATIVES (taste, claims, tone, tradeoffs the runtime cannot decide). A MEASURED FACT is banked without consultation, and a control this kernel treats as mandatory for itself is mandatory for every deployment it births: presenting either as a menu item pushes a governance obligation onto the operator as a preference, which inverts the kernel's purpose. (2) AN ANSWER IS A RULING, NOT A PREFERENCE -- an operator answer that settles a tracked question is banked as a decision record against the affected tracked_item ids in the same session it is given, so a successor session inherits the ruling rather than re-asking it. DECIDABLE PREDICATE: the turn that first acts on an answer contains that answer's text, and every tracked_item the answer settles carries the ruling in its record before session close.
environment_audit: MANDATORY before ANY install attempt or environment switch. Enumerate all available tools in the AI env (MCPs, connectors, scripts) and the OS env (all Python versions, pip variants, package managers, and fetch/VCS/shell tooling -- curl/wget/git/gh/jq/pwsh/powershell.exe -- with present/version/path across every host and subsystem the deployment spans). As session-zero Step 0 and in ENFORCED mode, run the governed `audit-env --json` verb for a deterministic enumeration. Establish ground truth BEFORE acting. Do NOT panic-switch on first failure -- exhaust the tool_fallback chain (S3a) first. HARDENED (S181, from E-090(a) and INS-042/INS-043): (1) ABSENCE IS A SEARCH RESULT, NOT AN ASSUMPTION -- a claim that a tool, file or record does not exist is a VERDICT, and a verdict from an incomplete lookup is a false verdict. LIST THE CHANNEL before declaring anything absent: grepping one file is not a search of the store. (2) THE AUDIT IS BANKED, NOT REMEMBERED -- its result lands in the RAG as known_issues/tracked records, because a newborn deployment does not inherit gotchas at init and will otherwise rediscover every one of them live, at operator cost. DECIDABLE PREDICATE: no install or environment-switch command may be the first use of a transport, and no absence claim may be issued without the enumerating command that produced it.
rag_portability: RAG_MASTER.json contains the COMPLETE behavioral ruleset for ANY LLM platform. No rule may exist exclusively in platform-specific storage. The project is transferable via the init prompt OR RAG_MASTER.json alone. HARDENED (S181, from BEHAVIOR-LAYER-SIDE-STORE-RISK and SPEC-DISCOVERABILITY-AT-INIT): (1) VENDOR UI CONFIG IS NOT A RULE STORE -- moving any part of the behavioral layer into vendor-side configuration (assistant instructions, skills, design surfaces, memory/past-chat toggles) creates exactly the second source of truth the drift auditor rejects, and it does not travel with the RAG. Vendor surfaces may hold POINTERS to governed state; they may never hold the state. (2) THE SPEC MUST SURVIVE THE BIRTH -- a RAG that cannot name the INIT spec it was parsed from is not portable, it is merely present: the completeness invariants self-skip on exactly the newborn deployments that most need them, so init MUST path-record or copy the spec it parsed into the RAG it writes. (3) PORTABILITY IS TESTED BY REPRODUCTION, not asserted -- the claim holds only if a fresh init from the recorded spec plus the RAG reproduces the ruleset. DECIDABLE PREDICATE: the spec-completeness check resolves a spec from the RAG and returns a real verdict rather than SKIPPED, and the drift auditor reports zero side stores.
session_end_protocol: HARD RULE -- SESSION-END RITUAL, run through the governed `session-end` verb, in order: (1) CLAIM-RECONCILIATION PASS (Rule 11 / INS-018) -- reconcile every published status-claim on the project's declared drift-prone surfaces (meta.reconciliation_surfaces) against its tracked records, and map every newly-resolved record back onto those public surfaces so the public view stays current; the closing audit mechanizes the surfaces it can resolve from the manifest, and this pass covers the un-mechanizable residual (natural-language claims no auditor can fully check). (2) CHECKPOINT -- merge the session summary atomically; the session-id increment persists HERE, not at boot. (3) ERROR_LOG FOLD + LOGGER CLOSE (KA-4 gate). (4) AUDIT, fail-loud. HARDENED (S181, from the S178-S180 gate work): (a) THE SEAL IS A GATE, NOT A CEREMONY -- session-end ABORTS rather than sealing on a red test suite or a dirty audit; this fired twice in S180 and is the difference between a rule and a mechanism. (b) XFER-PRESENT-GATE -- the seal is bound to EMISSION of a canonical-report pointer: a close that produced no verifiable transfer surface is not a close. (c) CLOSE-SEAL-ENFORCE -- an unsealed prior session blocks the next boot, which must run `session-resume` or close the prior id; `--force` requires explicit operator direction. (d) A NARRATED FAILURE THAT IS NOT BANKED IS A LOST FAILURE (Rule 8) -- every process error acknowledged in-session is written to ERROR_LOG before the seal. DECIDABLE PREDICATE: transfer_ready=true is reachable only with suite green, audit at 0 findings, a report pointer emitted, and the ERROR_LOG fold applied.
session_start_protocol: HARD RULE -- GC-FIRST CARRY-FORWARD RITUAL. At the very start of EVERY session (after session-zero), BEFORE any substantive work, in order: (0) BOOT-GUARD-FIRST-ACTION (KA-20, HARD) -- the governed `session-start` command is the VERY FIRST action of the session, before any other tool call, file read, or state claim to the operator. NEVER read the canonical RAG directly, on any transport and a banned sandbox least of all, to LOAD or REPORT boot state: `session-start` renders a deterministic BOOT-STATE BRIEFING (inference-ledger OPEN count + overdue flag, next_session_directive, backlog counts) that is COMPLETE for briefing the operator, so a direct read is an E-071-class tool_hierarchy violation and not merely redundant. (1) CARRY-FORWARD GATE, fail-loud -- refuse to start on an incoherent or unsealed inheritance and name the recovery verb. (2) GC DRY-RUN. (3) RULE DIGEST + OPERATING FRAME rendered into working context. HARDENED (S181): (a) ATTESTATION IS TWO-PHASE -- the session is not READY, and the logger is not opened, until `--attest <token>` is re-run and the token matches the LIVE operating_protocol digest; this makes rule-loading checkable instead of claimed. (b) AUTO-SID-DERIVE -- session-start DERIVES the next session id from meta.written_by_session WITHOUT writing it, identically in both handshake phases; the increment is persisted later, at checkpoint/session-end. No pre-read of any kind is required or permitted at boot. (c) REUSE BEFORE AUTHORING -- prior hardening is REGISTERED, not remembered: run the reuse-check verb against the asset registry (and the fleet view) before writing anything new. DECIDABLE PREDICATE: no substantive tool call precedes session-start, and no write occurs before the session reaches READY.
tool_contract: ALLOWED: read/list/write within declared roots, compute checksum, append WAL, rotate backup. DISALLOWED: write outside roots, overwrite source files, mutate without validation, bypass checksum, load COLD at boot without a trigger. HARDENED (S181, from E-090(b) and the guarded-verb migration): (1) EVERY CANONICAL WRITE GOES THROUGH A GOVERNED VERB -- add / un-add / add-rule / update-rule / note / priority / start / resolve / defer / reopen / discard / supersede / checkpoint. Hand-editing RAG_MASTER.json is outside the contract even when the intended edit is correct, because the atomicity, WAL append, checksum and .bak rotation are PRECONDITIONS of the write, not follow-ups to it. (2) THE INVERSE IS ALSO A VERB -- a pristine mis-add is reversed with `un-add`, never by hand: in S180 adding the first item of a new kind retroactively activated a coverage invariant across 67 legacy entries and took the audit from 0 findings to 64, and only the guarded inverse returned canonical state to exactly zero net change. (3) KIND IS A COUPLING SURFACE -- introducing the FIRST item of a previously unused kind can activate dormant invariants, so a new kind is a schema decision, not a labelling choice. DECIDABLE PREDICATE: after every write the audit reports 0 findings and HOT is byte-identical to .bak; if it is not, the write is reverted through the guarded inverse rather than patched forward.
tool_verification: Every session, before exiting BOOTING: confirm the transports the session will actually use -- governed file read/write, shell, browser if needed, and any project-specific tooling. A missing tool means walking the fallback chain (S3a) before halting, never improvising a substitute. HARDENED (S181, from E-081 / E-082b / E-086 / E-089 / E-090(d) / E-093, six consecutive sessions of the same class): (1) VERIFICATION IS EXERCISED, NOT ASSERTED -- run the `health` verb and put one real command down each transport; a transport that has not carried a command this session is unverified. (2) THE FIRST SHELL ACTION OF EVERY SESSION GOES DOWN THE PRIMARY TRANSPORT, so that transport failures surface at boot rather than mid-deliverable. (3) A BANNED TRANSPORT IS BANNED AS A CLOCK TOO -- the recurring breach was never a shell-access decision, it was the agent needing to let time pass and reaching for the only instrument it had. Waiting is a VERB: use the governed blocking `wait-for` (file + timeout + sentinel + bounded tail), which returns in ONE round-trip. (4) NEVER POLL A RUNNING COMMAND -- a poll-based result endpoint returns 'pending' while a blocking wait is in progress, so polling it measures nothing and spends the operator's metered resource. Launch DETACHED, chain the job and its wait into ONE command that writes ONE sentinel, and read it at the next natural turn rather than watching it. DECIDABLE PREDICATE: no result endpoint is called twice for the same command id, and no banned transport appears in the session log at all.
web_access_protocol: Web-retrieval method is a DETERMINISTIC first-match-wins decision, not a judgment call. Evaluate top-down and take the action of the FIRST true row: (1) target URL UNKNOWN -> use a search tool for DISCOVERY ONLY, capture the URL, re-enter from row 1 (search never delivers data); (2) a dedicated API / connector / MCP exists for the service -> use it, not generic web access; (3) the endpoint is retrieved REPEATEDLY, or the data feeds a pipeline or must persist across sessions -> a dedicated on-disk script saved under the project root [Tier 1]; (4) a ONE-OFF retrieval whose content must land ON DISK (binary, large asset, or input to a later tool) -> fetch-to-disk; (5) otherwise -> a single in-context fetch. HARDENED (S181): (a) A SUCCESSFUL FETCH THAT RETURNS A SHELL IS NOT A FAILURE TO RETRY -- a client-rendered page yields boilerplate with no body; that is a signal to ESCALATE to a JS-executing browser transport, not to re-request the same URL or to reason from the partial content. (b) A REFUSED FETCH IS TERMINAL -- content blocked by policy is not re-attempted through a different transport, a script, an archive or a mirror; report it and offer an alternative route. (c) AUTHORITATIVE SOURCES ONLY (Rule 13) -- vendor/primary documentation outranks summaries, and a live-verified claim outranks a remembered one. DECIDABLE PREDICATE: at most one retry per URL per transport tier, and any escalation names the row that triggered it.
